title: Power Exam Stretch
welcome_lead: Apply theories to voting behaviour and protest movements, then nail the exam evaluation.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology exam stretch on voting behaviour, protest and evaluating theories of power.
final_note: Strong answers join voting data, theory and a current event in one paragraph.

concepts.def: Voting based on social class background.
Voters switching parties more often than before.
Lack of interest in voting or politics.
Mass organised effort for change, e.g. BLM.

walkthroughs.body_html: Older studies showed strong class voting. Today, age, education and region matter more. Younger voters lean Labour or Green; older voters lean Conservative. This is partisan dealignment.

UK general election turnout sits around 60-70%. Some sociologists worry about apathy, especially among young people. Others argue young people simply engage differently — via protest, social media and movements.

State the view (pluralist/elite/Marxist). Apply with an example (Black Lives Matter, Extinction Rebellion, lobbying scandals). Counter with a rival view. End with a judgement on who really holds power.
